Bayesian Online Change Point Detection – "++" re-implementation

Source: R/hcp_bocpd.R
hcp_bocpd.Rd

Change-point detection with a native, self-contained Bayesian Online Change Point Detector (no ocp dependency). This is an adaptation of BOCPD (Adams & MacKay 2007) with documented innovations over the ocp backend:

  1. Autoregressive UPM. ocp uses an i.i.d. Gaussian underlying predictive model, which only sees shifts in level and variance. Here the per-run-length model is a conjugate Bayesian linear autoregression (a regression of x_t on [1, x_{t-1}, ...], Normal-Inverse-Gamma prior, Student-t predictive), so it also detects changes in dynamics (slope, trend, autocorrelation).

  2. Log-space + eps-pruning. The run-length recursion runs in log-space and the run-length distribution is pruned to the entries holding all but a fraction prune_eps of the peak mass – a bounded-state, streaming recursion.

  3. Surprise-based extraction. Change points are read from the Bayesian predictive surprise -log p(x_t | x_{1:t-1}) via a causal robust local z-score, replacing ocp's noisy three-list voting.

This mirrors the canonical implementation in the pyharbinger package (class HcpBocpd); the two implementations produce identical detections.

Usage

hcp_bocpd(
  hazard = 250,
  threshold = 6,
  min_distance = 15,
  burn_in = 5,
  order = 1,
  local_window = 20,
  prune_eps = 1e-06
)

Arguments

hazard

Positive scalar; the prior change probability per step is 1 / hazard.

threshold

Local z-score a surprise peak must reach to be flagged.

min_distance

Minimum distance between selected change points.

burn_in

Number of initial observations to ignore.

order

Autoregressive order of the UPM (regressors [1, x_{t-1}, ...]).

local_window

Trailing window of the robust local z-score baseline.

prune_eps

Run lengths below prune_eps times the peak mass are pruned.

Value

An hcp_bocpd object.

References

  • Adams RP, MacKay DJC (2007). Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection. arXiv:0710.3742.

  • Fearnhead P, Liu Z (2007). On-line inference for multiple changepoint problems. J. R. Stat. Soc. B, 69(4):589-605. (online inference with resampling/pruning of the run-length distribution; segment regression models)

  • Fearnhead P (2006). Exact and efficient Bayesian inference for multiple changepoint problems. Statistics and Computing, 16(2):203-213. (Bayesian linear-regression segment models)

  • Saatci Y, Turner R, Rasmussen CE (2010). Gaussian Process Change Point Models. ICML. (BOCPD with richer predictive models and run-length pruning)

  • Takeuchi J, Yamanishi K (2006). A unifying framework for detecting outliers and change points from time series. IEEE TKDE, 18(4):482-492. (autoregressive change-point surprise)

Examples

library(daltoolbox)

# Load change-point example data
data(examples_changepoints)

# Use a simple example
dataset <- examples_changepoints$simple
head(dataset)
#>   serie event
#> 1  0.00 FALSE
#> 2  0.25 FALSE
#> 3  0.50 FALSE
#> 4  0.75 FALSE
#> 5  1.00 FALSE
#> 6  1.25 FALSE

# Configure BOCPD detector
model <- hcp_bocpd()

# Fit the model (no-op; detection is self-contained)
model <- fit(model, dataset$serie)

# Run detection
detection <- detect(model, dataset$serie)

# Show detected change points
print(detection[(detection$event),])
#>    idx event        type
#> 51  51  TRUE changepoint
